title: A quantitative homotopy-interleaving gap over the cyclic-four group algebra
abstract: Over the group algebra F2[C4] of the cyclic group of order four in characteristic two, we give an explicit five-stage real-indexed persistence diagram F of unbounded chain complexes. Its stages are shifts of the periodic free resolution of the trivial module, on half-open intervals [i, i+1), with zero diagram before time 0 and from time 5 on. We compare three distances from F to the zero diagram: the homology interleaving distance (supremum over all degrees of the interleaving distances of the F2-homology persistence modules); the interleaving distance in an arbitrary localisation of the category of whole real diagrams at the objectwise quasi-isomorphisms (the derived category of real diagrams); and the strict homotopy-interleaving distance, which allows arbitrary finite zigzags of objectwise quasi-isomorphisms of both entire diagrams, including nonzero acyclic replacements of zero. The Lean development proves d_CohI(F,0) = 1/2 < d_IHC(F,0) = 1 < 5/4 <= d_HI(F,0) <= 5/2. So the three distances are quantitatively separated by a single explicit example. The lower bound for the strict metric comes from a fourfold defining-system obstruction for the resolution. The derived upper bound comes from a natural nullhomotopy of the two-unit shift. The upper bound 5/2 for the strict metric is witnessed directly, because every five-unit shift of F vanishes.
